Cap was $300. p2 overpays $310 for Marvin+Atlantic with no monopoly; p4 still holds Ventnor. $938 is what survives the oranges. Never sell Boardwalk. Watch if p2 tries to buy Ventnor."}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid or drop out in this Monopoly auction.

I have $938 cash. The current bid for Atlantic Avenue is $310, so the next minimum bid is $311. Winning would leave me with $627. I am weighing this against the threat of p1's orange monopoly with three houses on New York Avenue.

A $600 rent hit on New York Avenue would leave me with only $27. That is too risky. I should drop out.

Mortgaging my properties would raise only about $305. That is not enough to cover a four-house rent hit. I cannot afford the orange monopoly.

Mortgaging Atlantic Avenue would add roughly $130, bringing total liquidity to about $757. I previously set a hard cap around $300 and will drop out now that the bid has reached $311.

A single bad roll would force me to mortgage Boardwalk or everything. p2 is already overpaying for a single yellow at $310, but they still need Ventnor from p4 to complete the set and cannot build without it.

Two yellows unimproved yield only $46 in rent. p2 would overpay by $50 for a property they cannot build on. Dropping would bleed their $1,256 down to $946 and bring them closer to my liquidity. I am now weighing arguments for bidding $311.

Holding Atlantic gives me a yellow veto. No one can complete the set without trading with me. If p2 gets two yellows, they could pressure p4 for Ventnor and build a second monopoly. Three houses on yellows would cost $800 to $900 in rent. Blocking that trade is valuable. I still have enough cash to survive a $600 hit.

I am now weighing the incremental value of the yellow veto against letting p2 overpay. My assets include Mediterranean, Electric Company, and Boardwalk, but my dark blue set is blocked by p4. p1 has only $98 cash and cannot easily build a fourth orange house.

p1 rejected selling Vermont, so they remain the immediate threat. p2 has $1,256 and no monopoly; if they complete the yellow set, they would become the endgame boss. p4 has $513, owns Ventnor but not a full yellow set, and holds a Get Out of Jail Free card.

p4 previously dropped at $140 to keep Ventnor and block a cheap yellow set. That makes them unlikely to sell it cheaply to p2. If p2 gets two yellows, they will pay a high price for Ventnor. Holding Atlantic makes me the kingmaker. Both p2 and p4 need me.

Baltic Avenue is only thirteen spaces from the orange properties. It would take roughly two rolls to reach St. James Place, giving p1 time to build if they land there.

If I win, my cash would drop to $627. A $550 hit on Tennessee or St. James Place would leave me with only $77, forcing me to mortgage before the next roll. p1 has just $98 and cannot build a fourth house without receiving money from rent, trades, or passing GO. If I drop out, my cash stays at $938, which comfortably survives a $600 orange rent with $338 left over.

I have decided to drop out. My $300 cap is a hard rule. A $27 orange cushion is too risky. p4 might sell Ventnor for enough money, but that is uncertain.

I cannot bid $311 as a bluff. If p2 drops, I would win at that price. I will not raise without being ready to pay. p2 has been persistently raising, but they might fold if I match their bid.

p2 is trying to scare me off by framing the yellow bid as self-harm against the orange threat. They expect me to fold. I will not raise without being ready to pay. I will drop.

I will publicly drop out with a brief message that the price exceeded my valuation for a split yellow set. I will not reveal the orange survival math or my cash position. I want to avoid giving p2 a signal that I am afraid of the orange threat.
